plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure sets two congruent parallelograms side by side, outlined in dark blue with both diagonals drawn as thin lines, to place vector addition next to vector subtraction. In the left parallelogram the bottom edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing right and is labeled u; the slanted right-hand edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing up and to the right and is labeled v; and the diagonal running from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner ends in an orange arrowhead and is labeled u + v. The right parallelogram repeats the same outline, but its top edge is the one labeled u with an orange arrowhead pointing right, its slanted right-hand edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing down and to the right and is labeled -v, its bottom edge is also labeled u, and the diagonal that descends from the upper-left corner toward the lower-right corner is labeled u - v. Drawing both results inside the same shape shows that the sum and the difference are simply the two diagonals of one parallelogram. The pairing makes the point that u - v is built by reversing v and joining it head to tail with u.

interactionPlan.concept: The sum and difference of two vectors from a common origin correspond directly to the two diagonals of the parallelogram they define.
elements: Base parallelogram outline (thin dark blue lines, including both thin diagonals)
Vector u on bottom edge (thick dark blue line, orange arrow pointing right, labeled 'u')
Vector v on left edge (thick dark blue line, orange arrow pointing up-right, labeled 'v')
Vector u on top edge (thick dark blue line, orange arrow pointing right, labeled 'u')
Vector v on right edge (thick dark blue line, orange arrow pointing up-right, labeled 'v')
Vector -v on right edge (thick dark blue line, orange arrow pointing down-left, labeled '-v')
Resultant vector u + v (thick dark blue line on long diagonal, orange arrow pointing up-right, labeled 'u + v')
Resultant vector u - v (thick dark blue line on short diagonal, orange arrow pointing down-right, labeled 'u - v')

interactions.label: Vector operation
interactions.teaches: Switching to subtraction u - v is equivalent to addition of u and -v, which traces the secondary diagonal.

interactions.label: Construction steps
interactions.teaches: Building the vectors head-to-tail around the parallelogram reveals how the diagonals act as the sum and difference.

demo_steps.title: Vectors from a common origin
demo_steps.narration: When vectors u and v start from the same origin, they define the adjacent sides of a parallelogram.

demo_steps.title: Adding vectors head-to-tail
demo_steps.narration: To add u and v, slide v so its tail sits at the head of u. The addition path follows the bottom and right edges.

demo_steps.title: The addition diagonal
demo_steps.narration: The sum u + v is the resultant vector from the start to the end of the path, forming the main diagonal.

demo_steps.title: Subtracting vectors head-to-tail
demo_steps.narration: To subtract v from u, we add -v. We can lay this out by tracing u along the top edge, then -v along the right edge.

demo_steps.title: The subtraction diagonal
demo_steps.narration: The difference u - v is the net result from the head of v to the head of u, forming the other diagonal of the exact same parallelogram.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Vector subtraction visually connects the heads of the two original vectors, forming the second diagonal of their parallelogram.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Draw a single large parallelogram centered in the view, rather than two side-by-side, so the interactions can morph the vectors in place on one unified shape. Base outline and reference diagonals should be thin lines. Vectors should be thicker lines in dark blue with orange arrowheads. For subtraction, ensure the '-v' arrow on the right edge points clearly down and left (reversing the upward-right 'v').

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Toggle between addition and subtraction: the learner switches the parallelogram from u + v to u - v, v reverses into -v and the active diagonal changes, and subtraction becomes addition of the opposite vector.
- Button for construction steps: the learner steps through drawing u, placing v or -v head-to-tail, completing the parallelogram, and revealing the diagonal, making the result vector depend on the order of geometric construction.
- Click on a diagonal: the learner selects either resultant diagonal, that diagonal and its component edges highlight, and the relationship between each diagonal and its pair of side vectors becomes clear.

authoredContext:
Vector subtraction is similar to vector addition. To find u − v, view it as u + (−v). Adding −v is reversing direction of v and adding it to the end of u. The new vector begins at the start of u and stops at the end point of −v. See the figure for a visual that compares vector addition and vector subtraction using parallelograms.

Showing vector addition and subtraction with parallelograms. For addition, the base is u, the side is v, the diagonal connecting the start of the base to the end of the side is u+v. For subtraction, thetop is u, the side is -v, and the diagonal connecting the start of the top to the end of the side is u-v.
